analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bournemouth are perfect on 12 points and had won seven in a row in all competitions under Marco Rose by 5 November, while Celta (27th, 3 points) need a home win to get back into the top 24. Celta go to Real Madrid four days earlier and have a long injury list; striker Borja Iglesias's calf tear was put at about six weeks in mid-October, so he may only just be back.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower: Bournemouth have conceded only twice in four European games, and Celta's La Liga season has been tight (10 scored and 10 conceded in 12 games, with seven draws). Evanilson and Rayan are scoring off the bench for Bournemouth, so a narrow away win looks more likely than a shootout.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners. I lean higher: Celta had most of the ball and won 11 corners to 1 at home to Union Saint-Gilloise last time, and as the side needing the win they should push forward again. If Bournemouth score first, that pressure only grows.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. Celta's home loss to Union had only two bookings, and Bournemouth tend to keep control of games rather than chase them, so I see no reason for a heated night. The referee appointment, due nearer the time, could still move this.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Celta usually have the ball at home while Bournemouth carry a big threat on the break, so I see the total close to the site's figure. A Borja Iglesias return would add to Celta's side of it; his absence is the one thing pulling it down.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Celta put 7 of their 11 shots on target against Union and Bournemouth's attack is flowing, but Bournemouth also held Leeds to one shot on target on 31 October. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay close to 9.
